subject: Clarify: what we retain (requests vs outputs) and erasure evidence
messages:
From: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@brightbank.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@brightbank.com
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Data retention: what you keep by default (requests / outputs)

Hi Vivek,

Quick question as we complete our BrightBank security review: can you confirm Redwood's default retention windows and what is classified as a 'request' vs a 'generated output'? Our security team specifically wants to understand: 

- Default retention durations for user inputs (prompts) and model outputs (answers) for hosted API customers
- Whether streamed tokens (partial responses during a streaming session) are persisted beyond the session
- How KV cache artifacts or intermediate state are handled and whether they are archived
- The retention path and timing for deletion requests and the kind of erasure evidence you can provide

I've attached a simple matrix showing questions from procurement to make it concrete. Can you respond in writing (we may include in our vendor questionnaire)? If helpful, we're open to a quick 30-min call.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Bennett
Information Security Manager, BrightBank

Attachment: retention_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention: what you keep by default (requests / outputs)

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear matrix, and for looping in security. I can give a concise written summary below and then Karthik/Kimberly will add technical and compliance detail. Happy to schedule a short call if you'd rather walk through the items together.

High-level summary (short):
- By default we capture request inputs and model-generated outputs to support billing, debugging, and quality monitoring.
- We treat 'prompts' as the customer-supplied input payload and 'outputs' as the final model-generated content returned in the API response.
- Streaming fragments are retained only transiently during the session; the finalized output is what enters the capture window.
- KV caches and session-level internal caches are ephemeral and not archived as long-lived logs.
- Customers can request deletion/erasure; we provide an audit record of deletion execution and timing.

Karthik and Kimberly — tagging you to add the exact default windows and the evidence formats we provide so Sarah and BrightBank can close their questionnaire.

Best,
Vivek
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@brightbank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Data retention: what you keep by default (requests / outputs)

Hi Sarah, Vivek — adding technical specifics below to supplement Vivek's summary. I focused on hosted API defaults; Dedicated/Private customers can configure different policies per contract.

Default retention windows (hosted API):
- Customer-supplied inputs (prompts / request payloads): retained for 60 days by default. Purpose: troubleshooting, billing disputes, and quality analytics.
- Finalized model outputs (the response we return after generation completes): retained for 90 days by default to support downstream quality monitoring and regression detection.
- Streamed tokens (intermediate fragments while a streaming session is open): kept in ephemeral buffers; these buffers are not written to long-term logs and are purged automatically within 24 hours if a session is not finalized. Only the final output (if produced) is considered for the 90-day retention.
- KV caches and internal runtime caches: session-scoped, transient, and not persisted to the durable telemetry store. They are not part of the default logged artifacts.
- Aggregated telemetry and operational metrics (e.g., per-route latency histograms, token counts) are retained in aggregated form for 13 months for operational analysis. These aggregates do not contain full request or output text.

Deletion / erasure process and evidence:
- Customer self-serve: customers can initiate erasure of captured records via the Console (Requests -> Data -> Erase). For hosted customers, erasure typically completes within 72 hours and we return a 'deletion token' that references the erasure operation.
- Support-assisted: for customers needing us to perform deletion, we require authenticated request and an SLA window (standard: 5 business days) to complete.
- Evidence: we provide a signed audit artifact (PDF) showing the deletion token, timestamp, affected object IDs, and the operator ID who executed the workflow. For compliance reviews we can redact internal-only fields.

Residency notes:
- Data stored for the 60/90-day windows is stored in the region selected at provisioning. For EU-region customers the data is kept in EU-only storage by default.
- Backups: short-lived snapshots for disaster recovery may exist for up to 7 days; these snapshots are included in deletion flows where applicable.

If you want a one-page statement we can produce a compact exportable summary for procurement.

—Karthik
Director, Inference Platform (Applied ML)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Bennett <sarah.bennett@brightbank.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 May 2026 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Data retention: what you keep by default (requests / outputs)

Hi Sarah — adding compliance/commercial framing so you have language for procurement and InfoSec. 

Key points for your questionnaire: 
1) Definitions we use: 'Request/prompts' = any customer-supplied payload (text, files, metadata). 'Generated outputs' = the post-processed response we deliver back to the client. Streaming fragments are treated as transient; only the output handed back in the final response is persisted under the default capture window.
2) Default retention windows (hosted): inputs 60d, outputs 90d, streaming buffers purged within 24h, runtime caches non-persistent.
3) Residency: provisioned region controls residency; EU customers -> EU-only storage.
4) Erasure evidence: we provide a signed deletion artifact (PDF) + deletion token and timestamp. If you require chain-of-custody style evidence for an audit, we can produce an expanded report (standard turnaround 10 business days).
5) Contractual options: we support shorter retention SLAs (e.g., 30d/30d) for enterprise customers under Dedicated/Private contracts — this is handled as a contractual amendment with an associated SKU.

Attachment: redwood-erasure-playbook.pdf (high level runbook and evidence examples)

If BrightBank needs this formatted as an appendix for your vendor questionnaire, tell me the target audience and I'll tailor the wording.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Compliance & Security
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — this is exactly what we needed. A couple of quick clarifications before I close the questionnaire: 

- Can you confirm that the signed deletion artifact includes the list of object IDs (or deletion token) and issuance timestamp?
- Are backups explicitly covered by the erasure SLA or do they require separate tickets?

If you can reply to those two points (short yes/no plus 1-line clarifier) I'll attach the answers to our RFP. If needed, we can take the longer audit report requested by our compliance team.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Sarah
